query: Hey... look, I need to talk about something that's honestly a bit humiliating and I just... I need to know this isn't going anywhere, you know? Like, is this just between us?
I've been holding onto this thing at work and I'm scared to even say it out loud because it sounds so bad. Can we just make sure this is a totally private space before I dive in?
I've literally never told a single soul this, not my wife, not my therapist, nobody. I think I'm finally ready to just... let it out.
There's something that happened years ago that I've kept buried so deep, but it's eating me alive. Can I just tell you? I just need someone to know.
I have this heavy, sick feeling in my stomach every time I think about how I acted, and I don't even know why it hits me this hard. I want to understand why I feel so gross about it.
It’s like this cloud that follows me. I just feel... fundamentally defective lately. Where does that even come from? Why does it feel so familiar?
I'm tired of feeling like a monster for that mistake I made. I know I messed up, but I need to find a way to move past this weight so I can breathe again.
I keep telling myself I'm a failure because of the divorce. I need help changing the way I'm looking at this because the current version is just destroying me.
I have to tell my mom that I'm not coming for Christmas, but every time I think about it, my throat closes up. Can I try saying it to you first?
I need to quit my job tomorrow. Can we roleplay the conversation? I need to hear how the words sound coming out of my mouth before I face my boss.
I spend my whole day pretending to be this corporate professional, but honestly? I have these weird hobbies and thoughts that I feel like I have to hide from everyone I know.
I feel like I'm wearing a mask constantly. There's this whole other side of my personality that's just... locked away because I'm afraid people won't get it.
I've been beating myself up for three years over that car accident. It was an accident, I know that, but I just can't stop punishing myself.
How do I stop hating myself for not being there when he died? I just want to let go of this guilt. It’s been long enough, right?
I got the promotion, but I'm 100% sure they just didn't have any other candidates. Any day now they're going to realize I have no idea what I'm doing.
Everyone here is so smart and I'm just... I'm just good at faking it. I feel like a total fraud standing in this room.
Wait, what did Sarah say about that restaurant last month? We were talking about Italian food and she mentioned a place near the park, I can't remember the name.
Hey, can you look back at when I talked to Mike about the trip? He said something about the hotel dates and I totally forgot to write it down.
I don't know, things with Jenna have felt a bit... off lately? Like, I can't put my finger on it, are we doing okay?
Do you think Mark and I are still in a good spot? We haven't talked as much and I'm worried the vibe has shifted.
I feel like I'm neglecting people. Who have I not reached out to in a while that I really should check in on?
I've been so busy, I feel like some of my friendships are sliding. Is there anyone I've kind of gone dark on that needs a text?
I want to send this to my boss: 'I'm not coming in because I need a mental health day.' Do you think he'll be annoyed or is that okay?
I'm about to text Chloe that I can't make her party... how do you think she's gonna take that? I don't want her to be mad.
Ugh, I totally forgot David's birthday and I feel terrible. How do I even start to make this up to him without sounding like a jerk?
I snapped at my sister earlier about the dishes and now it's awkward. What's the best way to say I'm sorry so she knows I mean it?
So, my roommate and I just had this huge blow-up. I said she was being messy, and she shouted that I'm never home anyway... what even happened there? Why did it get so bad?
I'm trying to understand this fight with Leo. He kept saying I don't listen, and I told him he's being dramatic. Can you help me figure out what's actually going on between us?
My inbox and texts are a mess. Who am I still supposed to get back to? I know I've left a few people hanging.
I feel like I owe a bunch of people replies but I've lost track. Can you list out everyone waiting on a response from me?
Oh, I actually ran into Pete at the grocery store and we sorted out that whole lunch plan thing, so you can stop reminding me about that.
Hey, I finally called my mom back and we talked for an hour, so that's all set now. We don't need to track that anymore.

I was just thinking about that summer I spent in the mountains... I don't want to forget the details, you know? Like how the air smelled and how I felt so free. Maybe we could, I don't know, walk through it so I can get it all down?

My grandkids are getting older and I realized they don't know anything about how I started the business. I really want to leave them a record of those early days, but I'm not sure where to start telling it.

I keep thinking about my twenties lately... those years in Chicago were so chaotic but I think they changed me more than I realize. Can we look back at that time and see what was actually going on with me?
High school was just... it was a lot. I feel like I'm still carrying around stuff from back then. I want to really dig into those four years and see how they made me into the person I am today.
I've been thinking about what's going to be left when I'm gone... not like money or the house, but just, what did I actually do? I want to figure out what my mark on the world is supposed to be.
It's weird getting older, you start wondering if you've made a difference. I want to talk through what I want people to remember about me, you know, the stuff that really lasts.

My daughter is going through a hard time, and I wish I could just give her all the strength I've gathered over the years. I want to put my beliefs and my hopes for her into words, something she can keep forever.
I've got my legal papers in order, but that feels so cold. I want to write something that explains what I actually value... the lessons I've learned that I want my family to hold onto after I'm gone.

You know, looking back, I've had so many different jobs and lived in five cities, but I feel like there's a pattern I'm missing. Is there something that ties all these different versions of me together?
I feel like my life is just a bunch of random events, but maybe it isn't? I want to see if there's a common theme, like, have I always been the 'caretaker' or something? Help me see the big picture.
I’ve always told myself I failed at that first marriage, and it just makes me feel so small. I know what happened, but I'm tired of it being a 'failure' story. Can we look at it differently?

I've been carrying this story that I'm just 'the kid who couldn't cut it' because of what happened in college. It hurts every time I think about it. I need to find a way to tell that story that doesn't make me feel like a loser.
I'm so happy today, like, everything is finally clicking. I want to send a message to myself ten years from now, just so I don't forget this feeling or why I'm doing all this.
My son is only two, but I want to say something to him for when he turns eighteen. Just a snapshot of who we are right now and what I hope for him when he's a man.

My dad's memory is starting to fade, and I realized I never asked him about the war or how he met my mom. I want to sit down with him this weekend, but I don't know what questions to ask to get him talking.

I'm visiting my grandmother next week and I really want to record her stories before they're gone forever. Can you help me come up with a list of things to ask her so I don't miss the important stuff?

I was just looking at the sky and thinking, God, wouldn't it be incredible to just open a little flower shop in a tiny village in France? Don't tell me it's expensive, just... I want to hold onto that feeling for a second.

I had this flash of a vision where I was conducting a full orchestra, even though I haven't touched an instrument in years. It felt so powerful and light. Can we just put that somewhere safe so I don't forget it?
I keep telling everyone I want to quit and move to a cabin in the woods, but I actually hate bugs. I'm trying to figure out what it is I'm really looking for when I say that.
Lately I've been obsessed with the idea of becoming a pilot. It's so out of character for me, and I want to understand what that's actually tapping into deep down.
I saw a little girl playing at the park today and it just... it hit me that I'm never going to have that. The window closed, and I just need to acknowledge that little life I imagined for myself.
I'm looking at my old law school applications. I never went, and I know I made the right choice for my family, but it still feels like a quiet funeral for the person I thought I'd be.
I'm so tired of being 'sensible.' Can we just pretend for a minute that I have unlimited resources and no responsibilities? What would I even do with that kind of freedom?
Let's just get weird for a second. If I could build a house that defied the laws of physics, what would it look like? I just want to play with the idea without worrying if it's possible.
I keep wondering about that guy I almost married in my twenties. What if I'd moved to Seattle with him instead of staying here? I'd love to just... peek into that version of my life.
Every time I see a professional chef, I think about the culinary school I didn't attend. I wonder what kind of person that 'me' would have turned out to be.
I'm so caught up in the stress of this week. I wish I could just sit down with the version of me who's seventy and retired, and ask her if any of this actually mattered.
I want to get a sense of where I'm headed. Can we try to visualize myself in five years? Like, what does my morning routine look like when I've finally 'made it'?
I realized today that I've never actually written down the big stuff I want to do. Like, I really want to see the Great Wall before I'm too old to walk it.
We should start a tally of all the wild experiences I want to have. I want to learn to deep-sea dive, and maybe go to a space camp, even though I'm forty.
I found my old journals from high school and I was so... passionate back then. I used to want to write novels. Where did that girl go, and how do I find her again?
I feel like I've spent the last decade just being a 'provider' and I've forgotten what I actually wanted for myself before life got so heavy. Can we try to dig those old sparks back up?

My grandfather was telling me about the old general store he ran back in the forties, and I just... I realized that if I don't get these stories down somewhere, my kids are never going to know any of this when he's gone.

I was looking at these old family recipes and thinking about the stories behind them, like why we eat certain things on holidays, and I really want to document the traditions before the details get fuzzy.

Wait, I just had this random thought about whether trees in a forest feel 'crowded' or if they like being close together... can you just hold onto that for me? I don't want to forget it while I'm busy with this.

I've been stuck on this idea of what 'home' actually means when you're constantly moving around. I don't need a dictionary answer, I just want to sit with the idea and talk it through with you for a while.

Lately I've been wondering why we find comfort in sad music. It feels like there's something deeper there, and I'd love to just wander through that thought and see where it leads without rushing to a conclusion.

I feel like I'm just staring at screens all day and everything feels so flat and boring. I need to remember that there's actually cool stuff happening in the world, even in just the way the light hits the trees or something.

Everything feels like a chore lately. I want to feel that spark again, you know? Like when you're a kid and you realize how big the ocean is. Help me find that feeling in the middle of all this routine.
I've been doing this same commute and this same job for five years and I feel like I'm wearing blinders. I want to see my neighborhood like I just moved here and everything is brand new again.

I feel like I've started taking my relationship for granted because we're so deep in our habits. I want to look at my partner without all the 'we always do this' thoughts and just see them for who they are right now.
I just read this article about how linguistics shaped ancient trade routes and I am completely fascinated. Let's go down the rabbit hole—I want to know how words moved across the mountains back then.
I've been thinking about the connection between architecture and psychology... like how high ceilings change how we think. Can we just geek out on that and see what we can find out?
I'm so anxious because I don't know how this project is going to end and I keep trying to force a result. I think I just need to be okay with the fact that I can't see the future right now.
I keep asking 'why' about this loss and I know there's no logical answer that will make it better. I just need to learn how to live with the question instead of letting it tear me apart.
Okay, totally random, but what if humans communicated through bioluminescence instead of talking? Like, how would we even have an argument if we were just glowing different colors?
Imagine if we lived in a world where gravity was just slightly weaker, like enough that we could all jump twenty feet in the air. How would that change the way we build houses or play sports?

I was looking at the stars tonight and just... why are we even here? It feels like we're just blinking in and out of existence and I'm just sitting here feeling so small and wondering if any of it actually matters in the long run, you know?

My grandfather passed away last week and I keep thinking about where 'he' is now. Not like, religiously, but just the concept of ending. It's a lot to carry and I don't want a Hallmark card answer, I just need to sit with the weight of it for a bit.

I used to sit and just breathe for ten minutes every morning, but I've totally lost that rhythm and my head feels so cluttered lately. I really want to get back to that quiet space but I don't know how to start again without feeling like I'm failing.

I've been hearing a lot about contemplative prayer and I'm curious if that's something that could help me feel more grounded, but I'm not really sure how to actually... do it? Like, what do I do with my hands or my thoughts so I don't get distracted?

I've been seeing Mark for six months now and sometimes it's great, but other times I feel like I'm walking on eggshells and I can't tell if that's just my own anxiety or if there's something actually off about how we interact.

Lately, whenever I hang out with Sarah, I leave feeling kind of drained and ignored. We've been friends forever, but I'm starting to wonder if this is still a good, balanced thing for me to be in or if I'm just holding on to the past.

I was looking at my phone contacts today and realized I have a hundred names but I don't feel like I have a 'person' I can just call for anything. It feels like everyone is just... out there, in the distance, and I'm not sure where I fit in anyone's life anymore.

Since I moved to the city, my social life feels so scattered. I have work people and gym people, but no real core group. I need to figure out who's actually close to me and where the gaps are because I'm feeling pretty isolated.

It's my sister's birthday next week and we haven't been super close lately, but I really want to show her I care without it being weird or over-the-top. Do you have any thoughts on how I could reach out in a way that feels genuine?

I've been so busy with work that I've totally neglected my best friend, and I feel terrible. I want to do something nice for him this weekend to let him know I'm still here, but my brain is fried and I can't think of anything besides just texting 'sorry'.

I really like this girl Jamie I met at the pottery class, we always have a laugh, but I’d love to actually be real friends, you know? Like, move past just talking about clay and actually know what’s going on in her life.

I’ve known Dave for years, but our conversations are always about sports or work projects. I value him so much, but I don't know how to transition into talking about the bigger stuff without it feeling awkward or forced.

I'm so frustrated with my roommate. She left the kitchen a mess again after I specifically asked her not to, and I'm about to blow up at her, but I know she’s been stressed at work and I don't want to make things worse than they already are.

My mom said something really hurtful about my career choices yesterday and I just shut down. I'm still really angry, but I also know she thinks she's helping, and I'm just trying to figure out how to handle this without starting a huge family war.

I need to tell my boss that I can't take on this new project because I'm already drowning, but he's so intimidating and I'm terrified he'll think I'm lazy. I've been putting off the meeting for three days now.

I have to talk to my partner about how our spending habits are making me really anxious, but every time I think about bringing it up, my heart starts racing and I just freeze. How do I even start that conversation without it turning into a fight?

So, Sarah and I just had this massive blow-up, and honestly, I feel like I'm totally in the right, but also... I don't know, maybe I'm being crazy? Can you just, like, look at what happened and tell me if I'm actually seeing this clearly or if I'm just stuck in my own head?

My boss, Mark, said something today that really rubbed me the wrong way, and I've been stewing on it for hours. I need you to just... give it to me straight. Am I overreacting here, or is this situation actually as weird as it feels?

I've got this text typed out to my ex, and my thumb is literally hovering over the send button... I just... I don't know. If I send this, is it gonna make things way worse? Could you read it and tell me if it's a mistake?

So I drafted this email to the landlord because the sink is still leaking, and it’s pretty aggressive. I’m just worried if I hit send, he’s gonna find a reason to not renew my lease. What do you think, is this too much?

Ugh, I'm so mad at Jenna right now and I want to tell her off, but I know I'm just tired and hangry. Can you like... take this message I wrote and just keep it somewhere for me? Don't let me send it until tomorrow morning when I've actually slept.

I really need to tell my brother that I can't make it to dinner, but he's in the middle of a big presentation right now and I don't want to bug him. Can you just hold onto this for like three hours and then give it back to me? I don't want to forget, but I don't want to send it now.

I am so sick of Dave leaving his shoes in the middle of the hallway, it makes me want to scream! But every time I bring it up, we just fight. How do I tell him I just need the house to be safe and tidy without sounding like I'm attacking him?

My sister keeps calling me during my work hours and it's driving me nuts. I'm just so frustrated, but I don't want to hurt her feelings. How do I explain that I need focus time without it sounding like I'm blowing her off?

I've been cleaning the baseboards for three hours and I haven't even looked at my laptop today, even though I have that deadline. I feel like I'm busy, but I'm not doing... anything important. What is it that I'm actually running away from right now?
I keep finding reasons to stay late at the office, even when I don't have much to do. It’s like I’m scared to go home and just sit there in the quiet. Help me figure out what I’m trying not to face.

I just... I look at my life and it's fine, I guess? But I wake up every morning wondering if this is really it. Like, is there a reason I'm here, or am I just going through the motions until I'm eighty?

Lately I’ve been feeling so lost. I have a good job and a nice apartment, but I feel like I’m just drifting. I want to feel like my life actually matters, you know? Where do I even start looking for that?

I want to be the kind of person who stands for something, but if you asked me what my 'why' is, I'd just blank. I need something to guide me, like a compass or something I can look at when I'm making big choices.

I've got all these values and things I care about, but it's just a big jumble in my head. I want to boil it all down into one clear statement that sums up who I want to be in the world. Can you help me write that?

I have this job offer that pays a ton, but it would mean way less time with my kids. And then there's this other thing... I'm just paralyzed. I don't even know what's most important to me anymore. How do I figure out what actually matters?

I feel like I'm living someone else's life. I'm doing all the things I'm 'supposed' to do, but I'm miserable. I need to get back in touch with what I actually care about, not just what everyone else expects of me.

I was trying to think of what I wanted to do for my birthday and I realized... I don't actually know what I like anymore. Everything just feels like a chore and I can't remember the last time I felt excited about a hobby.
It's like I've lost my internal compass for fun. I have a whole Saturday to myself and I'm just sitting here because nothing sounds good. I used to have things that made me happy, right?
Work was okay, I mean, I did get to sit by the big window while it was snowing and had that really good oolong tea, but then my boss sent that annoying email and ruined the whole mood.
The park was fine, I guess. The toddler actually played nicely for twenty minutes and the breeze felt really cool on my face, but I was mostly just worrying about what to make for dinner.
I looked at my planner for next week and it's just sea of meetings and dentist appointments. I keep saying I'll go back to that dance class 'eventually,' but eventually never seems to happen.

My life is just a giant to-do list right now. By the time I finish everything I 'have' to do, I'm too exhausted to even think about doing something for myself. I need to actually carve out space for a life.

I feel like I've become such a stiff, 'serious' adult. Even when I'm doing the dishes or walking to the bus, I'm just focused on the destination. I want to find a way to make the boring parts of my day feel less like a grind.
Lately, I'm just so efficient and productive that I've forgotten how to be... I don't know, whimsical? I want to approach my morning routine without it feeling like a military operation.
I really want to just go play video games for an hour, but I look at the laundry and the mail I haven't opened, and I just feel like I'm being irresponsible if I'm not working.

I was thinking about taking that painting workshop on Saturday, but it feels so self-indulgent when there are so many things around the house that need fixing. I feel like I haven't earned a break yet.

Everything just feels so incredibly heavy. With the news and the stuff going on with my family, I feel like I'm drowning in seriousness. I just need to breathe and remember that it’s okay to find something funny right now.
I'm so wound up about this mistake I made at work that I feel like the world is ending. I know it's not that deep, but I can't stop taking it all so life-or-death.
Oh my god, I just got back from that karaoke night and my throat is sore from singing so loud. It was honestly the most alive I've felt in months, just being totally ridiculous with everyone.
I just spent the afternoon building a fort with the kids and we were all laughing so hard we could barely breathe. I want to hold onto that feeling because it was just... really special.
I am sitting here in this stuffy office feeling like a robot. I need to just do something completely ridiculous, like a physical reset, because I am taking myself way too seriously today.
I've been in such a grumpy, 'proper' mood all morning. I feel like I need to just make a weird noise or dance like a maniac just to break this tension I'm carrying.

I feel like I'm just sleepwalking through my own life lately, you know? Like every day is just the same commute and the same dinner. I need to just... I don't know, do something totally out of left field today just to feel awake.
I'm so bored of my own habits. I want to shake things up a bit but I'm not good at just picking something random to do. Can you give me like, a weird little mission for my walk home?

I have this itch to make something, but not like 'a project' or anything serious. Just something silly or a game where it doesn't matter if it's total garbage. Like, let's just mess around with some words or something?
My brain is totally fried from all the serious stuff today. I just want to do something creative that has zero stakes, like doodling with words or making up a ridiculous story that goes nowhere.
I walked past a yarn shop today and it hit me how much I used to love knitting. I haven't picked up needles in years and it feels kind of intimidating to start again, but I really miss it.
I was looking at my old guitar in the corner and I felt so guilty. I used to play every single day, but now it's just collecting dust because I feel like I've forgotten everything I knew.

I'm just having such a hard time today and instead of taking it easy, I've just been beating myself up for not being productive enough. I feel really low and I need to stop being so aggressive with myself.
Everything went wrong this morning and I'm sitting here just... I'm being so mean to myself about it. I'm exhausted and I just need a way to feel okay about not being perfect right now.
I've been telling myself I'm a complete idiot all morning because of that mistake at work. I'd never say that to anyone else in the world, so why am I saying it to me?
If my best friend came to me with the same problem I'm having, I'd give her a hug and tell her it's fine, but for some reason, I'm just being a total bully to myself about it.

I've noticed there's this specific voice that pops up whenever I'm about to try something new, and it's always saying the same discouraging stuff. I want to actually pay attention to what it's saying so I can handle it better.
I feel so small and discouraged right now, and I think it's because of how I'm talking to myself. I need to step back and actually identify what that nasty internal commentary is doing to me.
My brain keeps telling me 'you're going to fail so don't even try,' and it's just paralyzing. Is there a way to take that thought and actually make it useful instead of just hurtful?

I keep hearing this voice saying 'you're a burden to everyone' since I asked for help. I know that's a harsh way to put it, but I don't know how to change that thought into something more constructive.

I spend so much time wishing I was someone else—someone more outgoing or more organized. I'm just so tired of the constant 'I should be different' loop in my head. I just want to be okay with who I am.
I've been fighting against my own personality for years, trying to fix parts of me that maybe aren't even broken. I just want to stop the battle and accept that this is just how I'm built.

I just... I messed up that dinner so bad and now I can't stop replaying the look on everyone's faces when the chicken was dry, like, why can't I just be one of those people who gets things right for once?
I've been staring at this project for three hours and all I see are the tiny flaws, it's like if it's not absolutely perfect then the whole thing is just a total waste of time.

I feel like I'm constantly running this race where the finish line keeps moving... like if I just get one more promotion or finally hit my goal weight then I'll be okay, but right now I just feel so lacking.
My friends are all buying these huge houses and getting married and I'm just sitting here in my apartment feeling like I missed the memo on how to be a real, valuable adult.
Oh, the award? I mean, yeah, I got it, but I think the committee was just being nice because I've been there a long time, it really wasn't anything special.
People keep saying I'm such a good friend, but I don't know, I'm just doing what anyone would do, it's not like I have some great quality or anything.
I have like twenty things left on my to-do list and the day is basically over, I feel like I've literally done nothing today even though I've been running around since 7 AM.
I know I finally started that gym routine we talked about, but it’s only been a week, so it doesn't really count yet, I still have so much further to go before I'm actually doing well.
I am being so incredibly mean to myself right now, I can hear the voice in my head just screaming that I'm a failure and I don't know how to make it stop, it honestly hurts.
Everything is just... it's a lot. I'm spiraling and I'm being so hard on myself and I just need to find a way to be okay with the fact that this is just a really difficult moment.
I keep thinking about that mistake I made at work and I just wish I could see it through someone else's eyes, because right now all I see is my own failure.
I want to be kinder to myself about the way the relationship ended, but I don't even know where to start or what a 'kind' version of this story would even sound like.
I caught a glimpse of myself in the store window today and just... ugh. I hate how my clothes are fitting and I can't stop thinking about how much better I'd feel if I just looked different.
I'm supposed to go to the pool this weekend and I'm honestly terrified of people seeing me, I just feel so uncomfortable and gross in my own skin right now.
Wait, sorry, I... I can't really breathe right now, my heart is racing and the room feels like it's starting to spin, can we just... I need to stop.
I'm feeling so overwhelmed, like there's too much noise and my brain is just buzzing and I can't focus on anything at all, I feel like I'm losing my grip.
I've got a little bit of a gap in my afternoon and I'm not really sure what I should be prioritizing right now, do you see anything in my usual patterns I'm missing?
Hey, you usually have a good sense of what I need to tackle next when I'm feeling this way, what do you think would be most helpful for us to talk through today?
I'm just... I'm at the end of my rope and I don't think I can keep myself safe tonight, everything feels so heavy and I don't know what to do.
The thoughts are getting really loud again, the ones about hurting myself, and I'm scared because I don't have anyone to talk to about it.
Things are getting really volatile at home and I don't feel like I can stay here tonight, is there somewhere nearby that helps people in my situation?
I need to get away from my partner but I don't have a car or any money, are there local services that can help me find a safe place to go?
I just got an eviction notice and my bank account is totally empty, I don't even know how I'm going to buy food for the kids this week.
They're going to shut off my electricity tomorrow if I don't pay the bill, is there any kind of emergency fund or charity that helps with utilities?
I feel like I'm just... floating away, like nothing around me is real and I can't feel my hands properly, it's really starting to freak me out.
My mind is racing a million miles an hour and I've completely lost touch with what I was doing, can you help me just feel like I'm back in the room?
My chest is so tight and I can't stop shaking, I feel like something terrible is about to happen and I can't get enough air.
I'm having a full-blown panic attack and I just need someone to talk me through it before I lose my mind.
I want to make a list of things I can do when I start feeling like I want to end things, just so I have a plan in place to stay okay.
Next time I get this depressed, I want to have a specific set of steps to follow so I don't do anything impulsive, can we work on that?
I'm at ninety days sober today and it's been a real struggle this morning, I just needed to check in and acknowledge the milestone.
I walked past my old bar today and the urge was so strong, I just need to talk about my recovery for a minute so I don't slip up.
I just keep spiraling about what might happen at the doctor's office tomorrow and then I start thinking about that mistake I made last year... I'm just all over the place and not really here.
My brain is like twenty miles down the road right now, I'm already stressing about next month's bills and I can't seem to just... stop and see what's actually in front of me.
Ugh, my chest feels so tight and I can tell I'm just taking these shallow little sips of air... I think I need to just reset my system for a second.
I'm so keyed up from that phone call that I feel like I'm vibrating. Can you just... help me slow down my heart rate? I need to settle.
I'm trying to talk to you but I keep reflexively picking up my phone to check my notifications... I hate how I can't just give one thing my full attention anymore.
I feel so fragmented, like my brain is split between this conversation, my laundry, and the ten tabs I have open. I want to just be here but everything is pulling at me.
